title: Finance Controls Note: Card Balances, Cards per Purchase and the Daily Purchase Measure for Northgate Gift Cards and Merchandise Return Cards
content:
**Rule.** In the Northgate Gift Cards and Merchandise Return Cards program, balances on different cards are never combined, except that a Northgate Reloadable Gift Card's balance may be moved onto another reloadable card of the same holder where the card type allows the balance to be moved to another card of the same holder. Up to the card type's most gift cards usable as tender in one purchase may be used as tender in one purchase, and the daily purchase limit is measured across all cards bought by the customer that day.

## The daily purchase measure

The amount measured against a customer's daily purchase limit is taken over the calendar day of the purchase being evaluated. It is the total of the initial values of every card issued to the customer that day for a purchase of the card or for a business bulk order, together with the reload amounts the customer loaded that day.

| Kind of card value on the day | Counted in the measure? |
|---|---|
| initial value of a card issued for a purchase | yes |
| initial value of a card issued for a business bulk order | yes |
| reload amounts loaded that day | yes |
| initial value of a card issued for the refund of a no-receipt or gift-receipt return | no |
| initial value of a card issued for a promotion | no |
| initial value of a card issued for a protection plan claim reimbursement | no |

## Worked measure (hypothetical day)

On one calendar day a customer buys a Northgate Gift Card with an initial value of 30.00 and a Northgate eGift Card with an initial value of 20.00, reloads 15.00 onto a Northgate Reloadable Gift Card, and receives a Northgate Merchandise Return Card for a no-receipt return. The measure for that day is 30.00 plus 20.00 plus 15.00, a total of 65.00; the merchandise return card is not counted because it was issued for a return rather than a purchase or a bulk order. A purchase on the next calendar day starts a new measure.

## Balances and tenders

- Two cards held by the same customer keep two separate balances; one card's balance never pays alongside another's as a single combined balance. The one exception is a Northgate Reloadable Gift Card balance moved onto another reloadable card of the same holder.
- Several cards may each be used as tender in the same purchase, up to the card type's figure for the most gift cards usable as tender in one purchase. Hypothetically, a purchase paid with three Northgate Gift Cards uses three cards as tender, each paying from its own balance.
